fact: MINTTICS presented the National Cybersecurity Strategy on 2026-10-12, stating it was approved by Presidential Decree 256/25 of 3 December 2025.
The article states the Executive approved the National Cybersecurity Strategy in 2025; no day given, so as_of is the year.

Lei n.º 9/26 of 28 September 2026, in force on publication, creates a National Cybersecurity System comprising the Conselho Nacional de Cibersegurança, the Centro Nacional de Cibersegurança and a national CSIRT network; CERT.ao is the Centre's operational arm (PTI, 2 October 2026).

Lei n.º 9/26 requires operators of critical infrastructure, essential services, electronic communications, data centres, cloud and digital services to register with the Centre within 180 days and notify significant incidents to CERT.ao, with deadlines to be set by separate instrument.
Angola's telecoms minister writes that the National Cybersecurity Strategy, announced in 2022, was realised in 2025 (Presidential Decree 256/25 is named as held separately).
The minister writes that the National Cybersecurity Centre was put in place in 2025, and that it is to coordinate prevention, monitoring, alert and response.
PTI reports the Executive approved the National Cybersecurity Strategy in 2025, setting policies and priorities against threats in national cyberspace.

Presidential Decree 263/25, published in the Diario da Republica on 10 December 2025 and in force on publication, creates the Centro Nacional de Ciberseguranca, a public institute charged with preventing, detecting, responding to and recovering from cyber incidents, and approves its statute; the statute makes CERT.ao a department of the Centre.

Presidential Decree 256/25, published in the Diario da Republica on 3 December 2025 and in force on publication, approves Angola's Estrategia Nacional de Ciberseguranca; the text sets a five-year review and does not state a period for the strategy.
President Lourenço's State of the Nation address, as reported by PTI, refers to the approval of the National Cybersecurity Strategy and the structuring of a National Cybersecurity Centre.
Angola's minister said it approved its National Cybersecurity Strategy.
Angola's minister said it established the National Cybersecurity Council and the National Cybersecurity Centre.

O Telegrama states that Lei n.º 9/26 of 28 September 2026, in force on publication, sets up the National Cybersecurity System with a National Cybersecurity Centre for regulation, supervision and enforcement, and that CERT.ao sits within the Centre and coordinates the national response to incidents.

The Angolan cybersecurity bill, as reported by Portal de TI, says the country has no National Cybersecurity Strategy and no specialised bodies such as a National Council or National Cybersecurity Centre, which it proposes to create.
